item.title: Triality rotation of connections and Dirac operators on SU(3)
item.description:
arXiv:2610.12548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how triality, the symmetry permuting the three 8-dimensional representations of $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$, can also appear as a symmetry of geometric objects such as connections and Dirac operators. Take any Riemannian metric $g$ on the manifold $M = \mathrm{SU}(3)$ and let $
abla$ be a metric connection on $TM$. Using an explicit model of Clifford multiplication by deformed Okubo products, we combine spinorial lifts with isometries $TM \simeq S^+ \simeq S^-$ to show that $
abla$ can be rotated into two new metric connections on $TM$. So there is a canonical $\mathbb{Z}_3$-orbit of metric connections determined by $(g, 
abla)$, with no other choices. The three connections coincide when $g$ is bi-invariant and $
abla$ belongs to the Cartan-Schouten line, but in general they are different. The rotations of $
abla$ preserve the norm of the curvature, so they define a new $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetry of the moduli space of Yang-Mills connections on $TM$. They also preserve the Chern-Simons 3-form and adjoint Yang-Mills-Higgs functionals. After choosing an orientation on $M$, the rotated connections define three self-adjoint, Dirac-type operators on the spinor bundle. We prove that these operators are natural, in the sense that they commute with the Kosmann derivatives of spinors along all invariant Killing vector fields that preserve $
abla$. We also show that they are not isospectral, in general. This is verified by computing the simplest eigenvalue for the Levi-Civita connection and observing that it splits among the three operators as the bi-invariant metric on $M$ is deformed to one with isometry group $(\mathrm{SU}(3) 	imes \mathrm{SU}(2) 	imes \mathrm{U}(1)) / \mathbb{Z}_6$. Finally, we outline how the constructions in the paper may extend to general 8-manifolds with a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)$-structure.
item.dc:creator: Joao Baptista

item.title: Generic mean curvature flow has finitely many singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.12763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for a generic compact initial surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and any generic compact initial mean convex hypersurface in higher dimensions, the mean curvature flow encounters only finitely many singularities. This resolves the full generic Morse regularity conjectures of Ilmanen and Colding-Minicozzi-Pedersen in the above two cases. More generally, we show that if a mean curvature flow of a compact hypersurface has only multiplicity one spherical and cylindrical singularities, then after a small perturbation of the initial condition only non-degenerate cylindrical and spherical singularities appear.
item.dc:creator: J. M. Daniels-Holgate, Or Hershkovits, G\'abor Sz\'ekelyhidi

item.title: Compact Mean Curvature Flows from Non-Compact Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.12817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct compact, embedded solutions to the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ that arise from various non-compact initial data and exist for a finite time.
item.dc:creator: Theodora Bourni, Nathan Burns, Marcus Flook

item.title: Sharp lower bound of the first eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian under integral Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.12852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a sharp Zhong-Yang type lower bound for the first nonzero eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian on closed manifolds with small integral Ricci curvature for $p \geq 2$. The proof combines a global elliptic estimate obtained by Sobolev truncation with strict perturbations of one-dimensional comparison profiles.
item.dc:creator: Shoo Seto

item.title: Direct proofs for spaces with cyclic parallel Ricci tensor
item.description: arXiv:2610.12930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give direct proofs of rigidity results for gradient Ricci solitons, compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, and critical spaces with cyclic parallel Ricci tensor. For solitons and quasi-Einstein manifolds, successive traces of first-order pointwise identities yield quadratic equations for the Ricci tensor and its modification. These equations imply radial flatness and radial $Q$-flatness, respectively, and the corresponding global rigidity theorems apply. For critical spaces, comparison of two expressions for the Laplacian of the Hessian gives a pointwise tensor identity whose scalar contraction yields a weighted divergence formula. Integration then gives the vacuum static, CPE, and Miao--Tam conclusions. The same comparison also proves Ricci parallelism pointwise for solitons and quasi-Einstein manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Fengyuan Zhang

item.title: Generalized Gauduchon metrics on compact complex spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be an irreducible reduced compact complex space of dimension $n$, and let $\omega$ be a Hermitian metric on $X$. For each $1\le k\le n-1$, we prove that there exist a constant $c_k$ and a smooth positive function $\rho$ on $X_{\mathrm{reg}}$ such that $\ii\partial\bar\partial(\rho\omega^k)\wedge\omega^{n-k-1}=c_k\rho\omega^n$. The function $\rho$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero. The constant $c_k$ is unique, and $\rho$ is unique up to a positive multiple among bounded smooth positive solutions. We also prove that the full sign set $\{-1,0,1\}$ of the generalized Gauduchon constants $c_k$ on a compact complex manifold is preserved by finite sequences of blow-ups with smooth centers.
item.dc:creator: Yong Chen, Xi Zhang

item.title: Ruling out Infinite-Time Bubbling under $SO(4)$-Equivariant Yang--Mills Flow on $\mathbb{S}^4\times SU(2)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Yang--Mills flow on $\mathbb{S}^4$ restricted to $\mathrm{SO}(4)$-equivariant connections on the trivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ bundle. It was expected that antipodal instanton--anti-instanton configurations would lead to infinite-time singularities along the flow. We show that this does not occur. Moreover, for any smooth equivariant initial condition, the flow converges to the trivial flat connection.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Tribe

item.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.13405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(\pi_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the
item.dc:creator: Catalin Carstea, Matti Lassas, Tony Liimatainen, Leo Tzou

item.title: Isoperimetry of singular CMC hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We produce the first examples of singular isoperimetric boundaries with non-zero constant mean curvature in Riemannian manifolds. The main technical ingredient is establishing that, for constant mean curvature hypersurfaces containing isolated singularities modelled on strictly stable, strictly minimising regular tangent cones, weak strict stability implies local unique volume-constrained minimisation.
item.dc:creator: Kobe Marshall-Stevens, Gongping Niu

item.title: Compactly supported instability of Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.13507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On the Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metric of dimension $n\geq 4$, we show that the destabilizing TT tensor of Ozuch lies in the image of the ``TT-tensor machine''. By continuity, it can then be approximated, in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, by smooth compactly supported TT tensors, on which the stability quadratic form is still negative. This proves instability in the usual sense for noncompact manifolds. To our knowledge, no exact smooth compactly supported destabilizing TT tensor was known before, even in 4D.
item.dc:creator: Erwann Delay (LMA, AU)

item.title: Compact lcK manifolds with Gauduchon parallel vector fields
item.description:
arXiv:2610.13657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that on a compact locally conformally K"ahler manifold, the existence of a non-trivial parallel vector field with respect to a Gauduchon connection $
abla^t$, for $t
e  rac{1}{3}$, forces the metric to be either Vaisman (for $t=-1$), globally conformally K"ahler (for $t=1$), or K"ahler for all other values of $t$. As a consequence, we characterize compact Vaisman manifolds in terms of their Bismut holonomy group. Moreover, we show that in complex dimension two, the existence of a non-trivial $
abla^ rac{1}{3}$-parallel vector field forces the metric to be globally conformally K"ahler.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Moroianu, Giacomo Perri

item.title: The Renormalized Area--Willmore Relation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In [1, Proposition 8.1], Alexakis and Mazzeo showed that the renormalized area of minimal surfaces in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^3$ approaching the ideal boundary $\partial_\infty\mathbb{H}^3$ is the negative of the Willmore energy of their Euclidean conformal compactifications. In this paper, we investigate whether there are other geometric surface equations for which these two quantities satisfy a universal proportionality relation. We answer this question in the affirmative by extending the Alexakis--Mazzeo result to a broader class of geometric equations containing, as two distinguished cases, the equations defining generalized singular minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and linear Weingarten surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, for rotational linear Weingarten surfaces, we express both energies in terms of generalized hyperelliptic integrals and show that their doubles form a family of rotational tori in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose Willmore energies realize all values in $(2\pi^2,\infty)$, with a particular subfamily converging to the Clifford torus in $\mathcal{W}^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$, as the optimal value $2\pi^2$ is approached.
item.dc:creator: Alvaro Pampano, Aaron J. Tyrrell

item.title: Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
item.description: arXiv:2610.13746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By establishing a weighted Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality for maps which are close to a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling, we prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map in the case of finite time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Rupflin, Alex Waldron, Sebastian Woodward

item.title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.13848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in $R^3$ with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of two strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains two closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from the periodic solution of a Riccati equation.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Banks, Mohammad Ghomi, Hongda Qiu, Matteo Raffaelli

item.title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.13897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize the Hamilton--Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture. The public Lean declaration is reproduced in this paper. Its geometric interpretation follows, and verification is recorded in 4.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Liao, Ziyang Qin, Jui-Hui Chung, Ayush Khaitan, Zhengyang Zhang, Hongzhou Lin, Zijian Zhang, Ligeng Zhu, Peng Lu, Bennett Chow

item.title: The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In every sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$, with $n\geq 2$, we prove the existence of a global perimeter minimizer whose boundary is a smooth, non-characteristic, entire intrinsic graph but it is not a vertical hyperplane.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco Giovannardi, Simone Verzellesi

item.title: Large-volume fractional isoperimetry on products of closed manifolds and Euclidean spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.08556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a closed connected Riemannian manifold and let $\mathcal P_s$ be the fractional perimeter on $M\times\mathbb R^k$ defined through its heat semigroup, where $k\ge1$ and $0<s<1$. We prove that the straight cylinder $M\times B_R$, with $B_R\subset\mathbb R^k$ a ball of radius $R$, uniquely minimizes $\mathcal P_s$ among all measurable sets of the same volume, up to translations in $\mathbb R^k$ and null sets, whenever $R\sqrt{\lambda_1(M)}$ is at least an explicit threshold depending only on $k$ and $s$. Here $\lambda_1(M)$ is the first positive eigenvalue of the nonnegative Laplace--Beltrami operator $-\Delta_M$ on $M$. Under a larger threshold, the perimeter deficit controls both the deviation of the slice volumes from their mean and the square of the asymmetry relative to straight cylinders. For flat tori this gives large-volume uniqueness of straight cylinders for the periodic fractional perimeter, including singly periodic sets in every ambient dimension. The proof combines spectral reduction on $M$ with rearrangement of the Euclidean slices and a one-variable comparison between an interaction gain and a concavity loss.
item.dc:creator: Juneyoung Seo

item.title: Equivariant Steklov homogenisation and stability of spectral representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that isolated spectral clusters preserve their finite-group representation under equivariant spectral convergence. In particular, an irreducible limiting eigenspace cannot split into several nearby eigenvalues, while an isotypic limiting eigenspace imposes corresponding divisibility constraints on the multiplicities in the approximating cluster. We then construct a one-parameter equivariant Steklov homogenisation on closed orientable surfaces, allowing Laplace spectral representations to be transferred to Steklov spectral clusters. Applied to the hyperbolic surfaces of Fortier Bourque, Gruda-Mediavilla, Petri, and Pineault, this yields first Steklov multiplicities 16 and 21 in genera 10 and 17, and at least 24 in genus 37. These examples give counterexamples to Jammes's conjecture on first Steklov multiplicity.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Audet-Beaumont, Maxime Fortier Bourque, Alexandre Girouard

item.title: Coordinate-Free Automatic Differentiation
item.description: arXiv:2610.12776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automatic differentiation (AD) is a cornerstone of modern machine learning. Since all AD frameworks implicitly fix a basis of Euclidean space to define gradients and Jacobians, they natively process mathematical objects that are arrays of a fixed set of coordinates. This makes it awkward to express objects such as rotations, volume forms, and curvatures that arise, for example, in applications of AI to science. Bespoke workarounds lack reusability. We show that (i) a single, basis-independent derivative operator can represent many geometric differential operations, and (ii) this operator can be expressed entirely in terms of existing AD primitives. This reusable transformation can be composed with JAX batching, compilation, and hardware acceleration. Geometry enters as algebraic data. We experimentally demonstrate its reuse across different manifold operators, its composition through a spacetime inverse-problem pipeline, and its use in optimization over different rotor subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Alex Guerra, Joshua Aduol, Yaqian Tang, Daniel Williams, Ryan P. Adams, Peter Orbanz

item.title: Chern classes of Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.12785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct closed Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds with non-vanishing Chern monomials. For every $n \geq 2$ and $\lceil n / 4 \rceil \leq m \leq \lfloor n / 2 \rfloor$, there exists a $(2 n + 1)$-dimensional example of signature $(\lfloor n / 2 \rfloor, \lceil n / 2 \rceil)$ on which all Chern monomials with positive indices at most $m$ and total weight at most $n - m$ are non-zero in cohomology with real coefficients. Taking $m = \lceil n / 4 \rceil$ gives examples with $c_{1}^{\lfloor 3 n / 4 \rfloor} \neq 0$. For $n = 4$ or $n \geq 6$, the latter examples show that the Chern-class vanishing theorem for strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds does not extend to the Levi non-degenerate case. In these dimensions, their underlying manifolds admit no strictly pseudoconvex CR structures. The construction uses circle bundles over products of integral pseudo-K\"{a}hler manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Takeuchi

item.title: Brane space localization and genus-0 T-duality with $H$-flux
item.description: arXiv:2610.12825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a geometric theory on the brane space $S^2M=C^\infty(S^2,M)$ associated to a gerbe with connection on $M$. Normalized logarithmic holonomy around the latitude circles defines an average holonomy line bundle on the brane space, whose connection and averaged flux give an equivariantly flat superconnection. We prove that the completed periodic exotic twisted cohomology defined by this superconnection localizes to the twisted cohomology of $M$. This {\bf brane space localization} happens in two stages: circle localization lands on the free path space of $M$, and contracting the paths, after a correction of the twisting form, brings us back to $M$. Parallel transport along the meridians lets us average gerbe module connections, after which the circular iterated-integral construction applies. The resulting {\bf twisted brane Bismut-Chern forms} restrict to the twisted Chern forms on $M$; their variation is described by {\bf twisted brane Bismut-Chern-Simons forms.} For a T-dual pair, transporting the classical Hori morphisms through localization yields {\bf graded genus-0 T-duality} on brane cohomology. The composite of each morphism with its dual is minus the Euler operator in the level variable, so these morphisms are isomorphisms at every nonzero level. At level one these morphisms are compatible with the brane character and twisted $K$-theory T-duality.
item.dc:creator: Fei Han (NUS), Varghese Mathai (Adelaide U.)

item.title: Cohomology and multiplicative gaps for quasi-isometries of nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct two word metrics on the same seven-dimensional torsion-free nilpotent lattice whose asymptotic cones are isometric, but for which every quasi-isometry has multiplicative constant at least $1+\varepsilon$, for one fixed $\varepsilon>0$. We use a convex invariant of a fixed quasi-isometry $\Psi:N\to M$. The displacement cocycle of $\Psi$ and the right-invariant means on $N$ determine a compact convex set $\mathcal A(\Psi)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V_N,V_M)$. If $\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi)$ denotes the first-layer maps of the graded homomorphisms that occur as blow-downs of $\Psi$ with varying basepoints, then $$ \mathcal A(\Psi)=\operatorname{conv}\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi), \qquad\operatorname{Ext}\mathcal A(\Psi)\subseteq\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi). $$ For every extreme point $L\in\mathcal A(\Psi)$, the dual map $L^*$ is also the degree-one part of an isomorphism of the full real cohomology rings. This cohomological compatibility, together with the realization of first-layer Pansu differentials by invariant means, yields the multiplicative constant gap stated above.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Soumyadeb Samanta, Soumyadip Thandar

item.title: Minimizing tangent maps into complex projective space
item.description: arXiv:2610.13214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify all nonconstant smooth harmonic maps $\mathbb{S}^2\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ whose 0-homogeneous extensions are minimizing: they are, respectively, isometric embeddings or holomorphic isometric embeddings composed with a Hopf map.
item.dc:creator: Matilde Gianocca, Andr\'e Guerra, David Ziener

item.title: Finding the Birman-Series set
item.description: arXiv:2610.13645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By a celebrated result of Birman and Series, the set of simple complete geodesics form a nowhere dense subset of a hyperbolic surface. We show that a segment of finite length is in a (small) neighborhood of this set if it can be "extended simply" in both directions for long enough. We deduce that, for large enough genus $g$, there exist surfaces with a Birman-Series set that is roughly $\frac{1}{g^{\sfrac{2}{3}}}$-dense.
item.dc:creator: Peter Buser, Hugo Parlier

item.title: Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
item.description: arXiv:2610.13738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Jade Brisson, Bruno Colbois, Alexandre Girouard, Katie Gittins, Jean Lagac\'e-Taylor

item.title: Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
item.description: arXiv:2610.13747v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.
item.dc:creator: Joonas Ilmavirta, Teemu Saksala, Hj{\o}rdis Schl\"uter

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.13813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standing waves $e^{i\omega t}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $\Delta u+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Valentino Badalucco

item.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.13831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.
item.dc:creator: Gordon Heier, Ravi Mudaliar, Haotian Zuo

item.title: Lojasiewicz inequalities for maps of the 2-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2312.16686v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality $$ \left| E(u) - 4\pi n \right| \leq C \| \mathcal{T}(u) \|^\alpha $$ for maps $u \in W^{2,2}\left( S^2, S^2 \right).$ The inequality holds with $\alpha = 1$ in general and with $\alpha > 1$ unless $u$ is nearly constant on an open set. We obtain polynomial convergence of weak solutions of harmonic map flow $u(t) : S^2 \to S^2$ as $t \to \infty$ on compact domains away from the singular set, assuming that the body map is nonconstant. The proof uses Topping's repulsion estimates together with polynomial lower bounds on the energy density coming from a bubble-tree induction argument.
item.dc:creator: Alex Waldron

item.title: Isoparametric Hypersurfaces of $\mathbb H^n\times\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R$
item.description: arXiv:2411.11506v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the isoparametric hypersurfaces and the homogeneous hypersurfaces of $\mathbb H^n\times\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb R$, $n\ge 2$, by establishing that any such hypersurface has constant angle function and constant principal curvatures.
item.dc:creator: Ronaldo F. de Lima, Giuseppe Pipoli

item.title: Butcher series for Hamiltonian Poisson integrators through symplectic groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2503.05000v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We exhibit a new pre-Lie algebra in the framework of symplectic groupoids and, in turn, use Butcher trees to compute the Taylor series of a solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on any symplectic groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M.$ The impact of this new algebraic approach is twofold. On the geometric side, it yields algebraic operations to approximate Lagrangian bisections of $\mathcal{G}$ using the Butcher-Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and, in turn, aims at a better understanding of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of $M.$ On the computational side, we define a new class of Poisson integrators for Hamiltonian dynamics on Poisson manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Busnot Laurent, Oscar Cosserat

item.title: Urysohn width of hypersurfaces and positive macroscopic scalar curvature
item.description: arXiv:2504.06737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold with non-trivial codimension 1 homology with $\mathbb{Z}_2$-coefficients or $\mathbb{Z}$-coefficients has positive macroscopic scalar curvature large enough, then it contains a non-nullhomologous hypersurface of small Urysohn $(n-2)$-width. This constitutes a macroscopic analogue of a theorem by Bray--Brendle--Neves on the area of non-contractible 2-spheres in a closed Riemannian 3-manifold with positive scalar curvature. Our proof is based on an adaptation of Guth's macroscopic version of the Schoen-Yau descent argument.
item.dc:creator: Teo Gil Moreno de Mora Sard\`a

item.title: Weighted Lojasiewicz inequalities and regularity of harmonic map flow
item.description: arXiv:2504.07054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: At a finite-time singularity of harmonic map flow in the critical dimension, we show that a Lojasiewicz inequality between the quantities appearing in Struwe's monotonicity formula implies continuity of the body map and the no-neck property for bubble-tree decompositions. We prove such an inequality when the target is $S^2,$ yielding both properties in this case.
item.dc:creator: Alex Waldron

item.title: A Lower Bound for the First Non-zero Basic Eigenvalue on a Singular Riemannian Foliation
item.description: arXiv:2602.17501v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the paper, we provide a lower bound of the first non-zero basic eigenvalue on a closed singular Riemannian manifold $(M^n,\mathcal{F})$ having basic mean curvature that depends on the given lower bound of the Ricci curvature $Ric(M)\geq (n-1)K$ and the diameter of the leaf space $d_{M/\mathcal{F}}$. For foliations given by points, the results cover estimates of the first non-zero eigenvalues lower bounds, which are Zhong-Yang estimate, Yang estimate and Shi-Yang estimate. We also show a rigidity result that corresponds to the case of $Ric(M)\geq 0$. This is a generalization of Hang-Wang rigidity, which is the equality case of Zhong-Yang estimate.
item.dc:creator: Bach Tran

item.title: On Santal\'{o}'s Problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.01771v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates an isoperimetric-type problem posed by L. A. Santal\'{o}, concerning convex surfaces in hyperbolic 3-space that minimize total mean curvature among all convex surfaces with fixed surface area. This problem asks for a characterization of the minimizers and for the optimal form of a Minkowski-type inequality in hyperbolic 3-space. In this work, we propose a conjectural description of the minimizers under certain regularity assumptions. We also construct a new family of convex surfaces as as potential minimizer candidates and establish a property of the singular points of any minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Fang Hong

item.title: Doubly warped product Einstein metrics on spheres
item.description: arXiv:2606.05519v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a simple computer-assisted procedure to construct $SO(d_1+1)\times SO(d_2+1)$-invariant cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, and use it to recover known Einstein metrics on $S^{10}$ and $S^{12}$, as well as find new ones on $S^{11}$, $S^{12}$, $S^{13}$ and $S^7\times S^3$.
item.dc:creator: Qiu Shi Wang

item.title: Ambient and Poincar\'e metrics for CR $3$-manifolds associated with the self-dual Einstein ACH metric
item.description: arXiv:2608.29148v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct new ambient and Poincar\'e metrics for the Fefferman conformal manifold over $3$-dimensional CR manifolds, starting from the associated self-dual Einstein ACH metric. Unlike the classical ambient and Poincar\'e metrics arising from approximate solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation, these metrics satisfy Einstein-Maxwell-type equations to infinite order rather than the Ricci-flat or Einstein equations. Since these metrics are determined to infinite order without ambiguity, they enable us to construct CR invariant differential operators and local CR invariants involving arbitrarily high order derivatives of the Tanaka-Webster curvature and torsion. As an application, we obtain the ambient metric construction of the CR GJMS (Gover-Graham) operators of all orders in dimension $3$.
item.dc:creator: Taiji Marugame

item.title: Deformations of K\"{a}hler and Balanced Hyperbolicity
item.description: arXiv:2609.04816v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the deformation stability of K\"ahler and balanced hyperbolicity. We prove that K\"ahler hyperbolicity is open under arbitrary small holomorphic deformations, but need not be closed, even in families of smooth projective surfaces. By contrast, balanced hyperbolicity is not open in general: in every complex dimension at least five, we construct a balanced hyperbolic central fibre with non-balanced nearby fibres. We establish criteria for the deformation stability of balanced hyperbolicity using Aeppli cohomology and Lefschetz theory. For principal holomorphic torus bundles over products of curves of genus at least two, we compute the relevant hyperbolic cohomology, obtain a numerical characterization of balanced hyperbolicity, and prove its openness under small deformations.
item.dc:creator: Jixiang Fu, Jingcao Wu

item.title: Yet Another Family of Complex Structures on $S^6$
item.description: arXiv:2609.33826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Following a similar path as the recent construction of a complex structure on $S^6$ we construct another such family, disjoint from the known ones.
item.dc:creator: Wenfei Liu, S\"onke Rollenske

item.title: Compactness and Noncompactness for the Positive Yamabe--Escobar Problem with Minimal Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.08759v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Yamabe--Escobar equation prescribing positive constant scalar curvature and minimal boundary. The compactness conjecture asks whether being conformally equivalent to the round hemisphere is the only obstruction for its set of positive solutions to be compact. In this paper we show that this is true for dimensions $3\leq n\leq 14$. We show that this dimensional threshold $n_*=14$ is sharp by constructing in $n\geq 15$ nonumbilic and non-locally-conformally-flat examples of metrics in the hemisphere for which a noncompact sequence of solutions exists. We do the same for the special classes of locally conformally flat metrics, $n_*^{LCF}=18$, and the metrics with umbilic boundary, $n_*^{umb} =20$. In all three settings we also prove that the Weyl--umbilicity vanishing conjecture holds for $4\leq n\leq n_*$ and construct counterexamples in $n>n_*$ by perturbing the noncompactness examples. To the best of the author's knowledge, these are the first locally conformally flat noncompactness constructions for the positive-scalar-curvature, minimal-boundary case of the Yamabe--Escobar equation, outside the conformal class of the round hemisphere.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Cordero-Misteli

item.title: The Riemannian Convex Bundle Method
item.description: arXiv:2402.13670v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the convex bundle method to solve convex, non-smooth optimization problems on Riemannian manifolds of bounded sectional curvature. Each step of our method is based on a model that involves the convex hull of previously collected subgradients, parallelly transported into the current serious iterate. This approach generalizes the dual form of classical bundle subproblems in Euclidean space. We prove that, under mild conditions, the convex bundle method converges to a minimizer. Several numerical examples implemented using Manopt$.$jl illustrate the performance of the proposed method and compare it to the subgradient method, the cyclic proximal point algorithm, as well as the proximal bundle method.
item.dc:creator: Ronny Bergmann, Roland Herzog, Hajg Jasa

item.title: Nonlocal Characterizations of Stochastic Completeness on Complete Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.20205v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we first prove that the following generalized conservation principle holds on complete Riemannian manifolds: for every \(0<s<1\) and \(t>0\), \[ T_t^{(s)}\mathbf 1+\int_0^t T_\tau^{(s)}\mathcal R_s\,d\tau=1 \qquad\text{on }M, \] where \(\mathcal R_s\) is the intrinsic killing term measuring the loss of mass of the subordinate semigroup, and the condition \(\mathcal R_s\equiv0\) is equivalent to the stochastic completeness of \(M\). We then provide several new nonlocal characterizations of stochastic completeness. In particular, we show that stochastic completeness is equivalent to genuinely nonlocal conditions, including the zero-mean identity \[ \int_M (-\Delta)^s\varphi\,dV_g=0 \qquad\forall\,\varphi\in C_c^\infty(M), \] as well as the uniqueness of bounded distributional solutions to the associated fractional elliptic and parabolic equations. We also revisit the equivalent \(L^1\)-core characterization for the generator of the heat semigroup, which plays an important role in our approach. In addition, we prove \(L^p\)-contractivity and smoothing properties of the subordinate semigroup, establish both short-time and long-time asymptotic results for the fractional heat kernel, derive the short-time asymptotics of jump probabilities for the associated Markov process, and study the variational characterization and minimality properties of the fractional resolvent. Together, these results provide a unified analytic and probabilistic framework for the fractional Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Rui Chen, Bobo Hua

item.title: Geometry of the Atomic Condition
item.description: arXiv:2607.22782v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The class AC of integrands satisfying the atomic condition was introduced by De Philippis, De Rosa, and Ghiraldin in 2018. These integrands give rise to Almgren elliptic geometric functionals as proven by the second author and De Rosa in 2020. Explicit examples in intermediate dimensions include small class 2 perturbations of the area integrand and the recent anisotropies constructed by De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, among them the $\ell^q$ norms in Pl\"ucker coordinates for $q$ close to $2$. We reinterpret the atomic condition in terms of convex geometry. We also propose variants of AC, related to the SAC and USAC defined by De Rosa and Tione, which we call the exposed condition EC, the strong exposed condition SEC, and the quadratic exposed condition QEC. For integrands of class 2, QEC is equivalent to validity of a Caccioppoli-type inequality and is stable under class 2 perturbations; every such QEC integrand admits Lipschitzian normals. Combining these results with a result of De Rosa, Firester, and Tsiamis, we prove that a Lipschitz graph whose anisotropic mean curvature for a QEC integrand of class 2 is $p$-integrable, with $k < p < \infty$, is of class $\mathscr{C}^{1,\alpha}$ on an open set of full measure. Finally, for all $k \ge 2$ and $n - k \ge 3$ we construct strictly polyconvex integrands - associated to inner-product norms on $\bigwedge_k \mathbf{R}^n$ - which fail the atomic condition, showing that strict polyconvexity is necessary but not sufficient for AC.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Jakimiuk, S{\l}awomir Kolasi\'nski, Maciej Le\'sniak

item.title: Surfaces with nonpositive magnetic curvature
item.description: arXiv:2608.13534v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a negatively curved surface, magnetic (or twisted geodesic) flows with nonpositive ''magnetic curvature'' have a large-scale geometry on the universal cover that retains some features associated with geodesic flows: magnetic boundary and visibility, possibly magnetically flat strips. This has dynamical consequences: orbit-equivalence to the geodesic flow, density of periodic points, transitivity, entropy-expansivity, existence of equilibrium states.
item.dc:creator: Boris Hasselblatt, JinCheng Wang

item.title: Riemannian Shape Analysis of the Corpus Callosum in Kendall Space: Aging and Alzheimer's Disease
item.description: arXiv:2610.05326v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is a major white-matter structure and a well-established marker of brain aging, but most studies quantify it using scalar summaries that discard its boundary geometry. We present a Riemannian shape-space framework \cite{fletcher2013geodesic-regression} for analyzing age-related morphological change in the midsagittal CC, applied to the OASIS-1 cohort. Each contour is represented by $128$ landmarks and embedded into Kendall shape space, where translation, rotation, and scale are removed. We derive a multivariate geodesic regression with exact Riemannian gradients and use the fitted age-velocity field to localize age-related deformation to five anatomical sub-regions. In the cognitively normal cohort ($n = 252$), geodesic regression outperforms the Euclidean linear benchmark ($R^2 = 0.1355$ vs.\ $0.1216$). Regional energy is anterior-dominant: the Genu carries $46.1\%$ and the Anterior Body $23.3\%$ of total age-related shape change, together accounting for $\sim 69\%$ despite comprising only $\sim 41\%$ of landmarks. Signed projections confirm the ordering (Genu $r = 0.562$; Anterior Body $r = 0.507$). In contrast, age explains less than $0.5\%$ of shape variance in Alzheimer's disease ($n = 88$), indicating that the disease disrupts the healthy aging trajectory. A tangent-space classifier achieves an age-group AUC of $0.791$ from the 2D contour alone, exceeding a recent volumetric benchmark ($0.67$).
item.dc:creator: Olakunle S. Abawonse, Fatou Fall

item.title: Oblique boundary value problems for n-1type augmented Hessian equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.11400v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the global regularity of oblique boundary value problems for n-1 type augmented Hessian equations on a bounded domain, without imposing any convexity condition either on the domain or on the matrix-valued function in the n-1 type augmented Hessian equations. We establish a global existence and uniqueness theory for classical elliptic solutions by deriving global a priori estimates up to second-order derivatives. Besides the known applications for n-1 type Monge-Ampere operators in optimal transportation and geometric optics, the general theory here embraces equations raised by Li-Sheng, Some Dirichlet problems arising from conformal geometry. Pac. J. Math. 251, 2011, 337-359 and Guan-Qiu-Yuan, Fully nonlinear elliptic equations for conformal deformations of Chern-Ricci forms. Adv. Math. 343, 2019, 538-566.
item.dc:creator: Zhibo Hu, Feida Jiang
